title: Fractional Equations That Reduce to Quadratic Equations
seo_title: Sec 3 Fractional equations Worksheets: Free Secondary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: solving fractional equations that can be reduced to quadratic equations such as 6/(x + 4) = 3 + x and 1/(x − 2) + 2/(x − 3) = 5
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 maths worksheets on fractional equations that reduce to quadratic equations: clearing denominators, solving by factorisation or formula, excluded values and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply every term by the denominators, then solve the quadratic.
key_sub: Reject any answer that makes a denominator 0 or does not make sense.
body_html:
How it works

  • Multiply every term by the denominators (the lowest common multiple of them) to clear the fractions.
  • Expand, collect all terms on one side and solve the quadratic by factorising or the formula.
  • Check each answer: a value that makes a denominator 0 is not allowed. In word problems, also reject answers that do not make sense.
Example

Solve 6x + 4 = 3 + x.

Multiply by (x + 4): 6 = (3 + x)(x + 4)

x² + 7x + 6 = 0, so (x + 1)(x + 6) = 0

Answer: x = −6 or x = −1

Example

Solve 1x + 2x + 1 = 1.

Multiply by x(x + 1): (x + 1) + 2x = x(x + 1)

x² − 2x − 1 = 0, so x = 1 ± √2

Answer: x = −0.41 or x = 2.41

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying only the fractions by the denominator and forgetting the whole-number term.
  • Expanding a minus sign wrongly: −2(x − 3) = −2x + 6.
  • Keeping an answer that makes a denominator 0.
  • In speed problems, subtracting the times the wrong way round. The slower journey takes longer.

faq.a: An equation with the unknown in a denominator, such as 6/(x + 4) = 3 + x. Clearing the fractions often turns it into a quadratic equation.

faq.q: How do you clear the fractions?
faq.a: Multiply every term on both sides by the product (or LCM) of the denominators, then expand and simplify.

faq.q: Why must I check my answers?
faq.a: Multiplying by an expression with x can bring in a value that makes a denominator 0. That value is not a solution and must be rejected.

faq.q: How do I set up a speed word problem?
faq.a: Write each time as distance ÷ speed. The difference between the two times gives the equation, for example 120/x − 120/(x + 10) = 1/2.

sets.title: Two fractions: forming and solving the quadratic

items.q: When 2x − 1 + 1x = −2 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by x(x − 1): 2(x) + 1(x − 1) = −2x(x − 1). Collect terms: 2x2 + x − 1 = 0.

items.q: When 5x + 1 − 2x + 3 = 2 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by (x + 1)(x + 3): 5(x + 3) − 2(x + 1) = 2(x + 1)(x + 3). Collect terms: 2x2 + 5x − 7 = 0.

items.q: When 5x + 2 − 6x + 3 = 2 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?

items.q: When 5x − 4 − 3x + 4 = 1 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?

items.q: When 1x − 4 + 6x = 1 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?

items.q: When −2x + 4 − 6x + 3 = 3 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?

items.q: When 5x + 6x − 3 = 4 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?

items.q: When 4x − 3 + 3x − 4 = −3 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?

items.q: Solve x = −2x + 3x.
items.e: Multiply both sides by x: x2 = −2x + 3, so x2 + 2x − 3 = 0 and x = −3 or x = 1.

items.q: A student solves x2x − 1 = 1x − 1 and gets x = −1 or x = 1. Which answer must be rejected?
items.e: x = 1 makes x − 1 = 0, and you cannot divide by 0. The solution is x = −1 only. Reject x = 1.

items.q: Which values of x are not allowed in 6x − 5 + 6x + 2 = 3?
items.e: A denominator cannot be 0. x − 5 = 0 gives x = 5, and x + 2 = 0 gives x = −2: x = −2 and x = 5.

items.q: A group of x friends share the cost of a $572 gift equally. If 2 of them drop out, each of the others pays $8 more. How many friends were there at first?

items.q: Wei Ling drives 360 km at x km/h. If she drove 5 km/h faster, the journey would take 1 hour less. Which equation is correct, and what is x?
c: 360x + 360x + 5 = 1, so x = 35
360x + 5 − 360x = 1, so x = 45
360x − 360x + 5 = 60, so x = 20
360x − 360x + 5 = 1, so x = 40
items.e: Time = distance ÷ speed. The slower time minus the faster time is 1 h. Clearing denominators gives a quadratic with a positive root x = 40 (360 ÷ 40 − 360 ÷ 45 = 1).

items.e: 1320x − 6 − 1320x = 2. Clearing denominators gives a quadratic in x whose positive root is $66 (20 books at $66, or 22 at $60).

items.e: 264x − 2 − 264x = 1. Clearing denominators gives a quadratic in x whose positive root is $24 (11 books at $24, or 12 at $22).

items.q: A group of x friends share the cost of a $126 gift equally. If 2 of them drop out, each of the others pays $4 more. How many friends were there at first?
items.e: 126x − 2 − 126x = 4. Multiply by x(x − 2) and simplify: 4x2 − 8x − 252 = 0. The positive answer is 9.

items.q: Jia Hui drives 60 km at x km/h. If she drove 15 km/h faster, the journey would take 20 minutes less. Which equation is correct, and what is x?
c: 60x + 15 − 60x = 13, so x = 60
60x + 60x + 15 = 13, so x = 30
60x − 60x + 15 = 13, so x = 45
60x − 60x + 15 = 20, so x = 22
items.e: Time = distance ÷ speed. The slower time minus the faster time is 13 h. Clearing denominators gives a quadratic with a positive root x = 45 (60 ÷ 45 − 60 ÷ 60 = 13).

75x + 75x + 15 = 14, so x = 45
